title: Giant third-order nonlinearity amplifies second-harmonic transport in Ca3Ru2O7
authors: Subin Mali, Yufei Zhao, Yu Wang, Binghai Yan, Zhiqiang Mao
abstract: Nonlinear electrical transport enables the conversion and detection of electromagnetic signals, supporting wireless energy harvesting, sensing and frequency conversion. Achieving both a large response and electrical tunability remains a central materials challenge. Here we harness giant third-order nonlinearity to amplify and electrically control second-harmonic transport in the correlated polar metal Ca3Ru2O7. Superposing a dc bias on an ac excitation enhances the second-harmonic signal by more than an order of magnitude. The bias controls the polarity of the induced response and activates channels forbidden by symmetry at zero bias. Both transverse and longitudinal components scale quadratically with the ac excitation and are odd in the dc bias, with angular dependences consistent with third-order conductivity. The underlying third-harmonic electric-field responsivity reaches 4.5 \times 10-6 m2V-2 at 3 K, providing a quantitative measure of the strong nonlinearity. The induced response emerges below the spin-reorientation transition near 48 K, linking its enhancement to the reconstructed low-temperature electronic state. Theoretical calculations identify quantum-geometric contributions to the nonlinear conductivity and reproduce the observed response symmetry. These results demonstrate how strong higher-order nonlinearity can amplify an effective second-order response, providing a route to electrically tunable nonlinear transport in correlated materials.
summary: The authors demonstrate that the second-harmonic transport in the correlated material Ca3Ru2O7 is governed by a giant third-order nonlinearity, which is controllable via an applied DC bias. This strong nonlinear response is intrinsically linked to the material's electronic reconstruction occurring below a specific transition temperature. The findings establish a pathway for electrically tuning nonlinear optical responses in correlated topological materials.
main_problem: To investigate how strong higher-order nonlinearity can amplify an effective second-order response, providing a route to electrically tunable nonlinear transport in correlated materials.
main_result: The dc-field-induced second-harmonic transport in Ca3Ru2O7 is shown to arise from its third-order nonlinear conductivity, which is strongly enhanced by the material's low-temperature electronic reconstruction.
method: The study combines electrical transport measurements (measuring second-harmonic voltage response under dc bias) with theoretical calculations (DFT+U) to model the nonlinear conductivity tensor.
model_or_system: The physical system is Ca3Ru2O7 (CRO), a correlated polar metal. The analysis focuses on the nonlinear current density described by a third-order tensor, $\mathbf{j}_i^{2\omega} \propto \sigma_{i;jkl}^{(3)} E_j^{\omega} E_k^{\omega} E_{l}^{	ext{dc}}$.
key_observables: Second-harmonic voltage response ($\mathbf{V}^{2\omega}$), third-order conductivity ($\sigma^{(3)}$), and the temperature dependence of the response relative to the spin-reorientation transition ($T_S \approx 48 	ext{ K}$).
important_parameters: The third-harmonic electric-field responsivity reaches $4.5 	imes 10^{-6} 	ext{ m}^2	ext{V}^{-2}$ at $3 	ext{ K}$. The enhancement factor of the second-harmonic signal is reported to be $>10$ times.
main_assumptions: The enhancement mechanism is attributed to the reconstruction of the low-energy electronic state below $T_S$, which modifies the underlying third-order conductivity tensor.
figures_summary: Figures show device geometry and magnetoresistance, alongside temperature-dependent resistivity and the dc-bias-induced second-harmonic response. Angular dependence studies map out the symmetry-allowed components of the nonlinear response.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context of nonlinear transport, details the experimental measurements of the second-harmonic response in CRO, analyzes the scaling and angular dependence to confirm its origin in third-order conductivity, and concludes by linking this giant nonlinearity to the correlated electronic reconstruction.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates how strong electronic correlations can manifest as giant, electrically tunable nonlinear responses, providing a platform for studying emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
